## Today

1. A short word on **environment variables** — you're about to need an API key
2. **Open class time** on the Census API and unit of analysis challenges

## Keys don't belong in code {.dark background-color="#022F4A"}

[The Census API hands you a key. **Don't paste it into a notebook.**]{.statement}

<br>

[Once a key is committed, it's in the git history forever — and your repo is public.]{.orange}

## The short version

::: {.cards}
::: {.card}
[Locally]{.card-title}

Put it in a `.env` file, add `.env` to `.gitignore`, load it with `python-dotenv`.
:::
::: {.card}
[On Databricks]{.card-title}

Store it as a **Unity Catalog secret**, read it with `dbutils.secrets.get()`.
:::
::: {.card}
[Always]{.card-title}

Never `print()` a key. If one leaks, **rotate it first**, clean up after.
:::
:::

**Full walkthrough:** [Keep Your Secrets Out of Your Code](topics/env_variables.html) — setup for Python, Databricks and R.
